01Interview Process

Interview ka Process

System design interview me koi ek "sahi jawab" nahi hota — interviewer tumhari soch ka tareeka dekhta hai. Repo 3 phases batata hai: pehle problem ko scope karo, phir abstract design banao, phir bottlenecks dhoondho aur suljhao.

Phase 1 — Problem ko scope karo

Kabhi assume mat karo. Pehle clarifying questions poochho — constraints aur use cases samjho. Do cheezein tay karo:

  • Requirements clarifications — system kis kaam ke liye hai, kaun use karega, kitne users, read-heavy hai ya write-heavy, kya features chahiye aur kya nahi chahiye (scope se bahar kya hai, ye bhi batao).
  • System interface definition — APIs tay karo: kaun se endpoints, kya parameters, kya return karenge. Isse interviewer ko pata chalta hai ki tumne problem ko soch kar toda hai.

Phase 2 — Abstract design sketch karo

Ab system ke building blocks banao aur unke beech ke relationships dikhao. Steps:

  • Back-of-the-envelope estimation — users, requests per second, storage, bandwidth ka rough hisaab (ye Lab 6 me practice karo).
  • Defining data model — kaun si tables/collections, kya fields, SQL ya NoSQL aur kyun.
  • High-level design — client, load balancer, app servers, cache, database, queue — ek diagram me poora flow.

Phase 3 — Bottlenecks dhoondho aur suljhao

Design kabhi pehli baar me perfect nahi hota. Scalable design ke fundamental principles lagao:

  • Detailed design — har component me gehrai me jao: caching kahan, sharding kaise, consistency kya hogi.
  • Identifying and resolving bottlenecks — single point of failure kahan hai? Database hot spot banega? Read path slow kyun hoga? Har bottleneck ka trade-off batao.
Yaad rakhne wali baat: Interviewer ko apni soch bol kar sunao — chup chaap diagram mat banao. Har decision ke peeche "kyun" batao, aur trade-offs khud hi point out karo.
SOURCESource: README.md
02Basics

Distributed Systems ki Key Characteristics

Koi bhi bada system design karne se pehle 5 characteristics samajh lo — scalability, reliability, availability, efficiency, serviceability. Har design decision inme se kisi ek ko behtar ya bura karta hai.

Scalability — Badhti demand sambhalna

System ki capability hai ki wo badhti hui demand ke saath grow kare aur kaam karta rahe. Do tareeke:

  • Horizontal scaling — pool me aur servers jodo. Aaj ke zamane me ye standard hai: load balancer ke peeche N servers, demand badhe to N+10.
  • Vertical scaling — existing server me aur CPU/RAM/storage jodo. Isme downtime aata hai aur ek upper limit hoti hai — ek machine kitni bhi badi ho, ek hadd ke baad aur badi nahi ho sakti.

Reliability — Fail hone par bhi chalna

Reliability matlab: ek diye gaye period me system fail hone ki probability kitni kam hai. Distributed system reliable tab hai jab ek ya zyada components fail hone par bhi service chalti rahe. Ye redundancy se milti hai — critical components aur data ki duplication, har single point of failure ko hatao.

Availability — Kitne time up raha

Availability matlab: ek specific period me system apna required function karne ke liye kitne time operational raha. Percentage me measure hoti hai.

AvailabilitySaalaana downtime
99% (two nines)~3.65 din
99.9% (three nines)~8.76 ghante
99.99% (four nines)~52.6 minute
99.999% (five nines)~5.26 minute

Reliable system available hota hai, lekin available system zaroori nahi ki reliable ho. Example: ek system jisme security hole hai — jab tak attack nahi hota, wo available hai, lekin reliable nahi hai.

Efficiency — Latency aur Bandwidth

  • Latency — response time: pehla data milne me kitni der lagi.
  • Bandwidth — throughput: ek diye gaye time me kitna data deliver hua.

Dono alag cheezein hain: ek highway chaudi (high bandwidth) ho sakti hai lekin toll plaza par rukawat (high latency) ho sakti hai. Interview me dono alag-alag discuss karo.

Serviceability / Manageability

System ko operate aur maintain karna kitna aasan hai — repair ya maintain kitni simplicity aur speed se ho sakta hai. Debugging, monitoring, deployment aur rollback isi me aate hain. Interview me log ise bhool jaate hain, lekin real systems me ye sabse zyada time khata hai.

SOURCESource: basics/key-characteristics.md
03Basics

Load Balancing

Load balancer ka kaam hai traffic ko servers ke beech baantna taaki system horizontally scale kar sake. Ek server par saara load aaye to wo mar jayega — LB use fail hone se bachata hai aur naye servers jodne ka rasta deta hai.

Load balancer kahan lagta hai

  • User aur web server ke beech — sabse common jagah, public traffic baantna.
  • Web servers aur internal platform layer ke beech — application servers aur cache servers ke beech.
  • Internal platform layer aur database ke beech — read replicas ke beech reads baantna.

Algorithms — Kaun sa request kahan jaye

  • Round robin — requests ko servers ko baari-baari do. Simple hai, lekin ye nahi dekhta ki kaun sa server busy hai.
  • Weighted round robin — powerful servers ko zyada weight, requests unke hisaab se baanto.
  • Least connection — jis server par sabse kam active connections hain, use request do. Long-lived connections ke liye best.
  • Least response time — jo server sabse tez jawab de raha hai, use zyada traffic do.
  • Least bandwidth — jo server sabse kam bandwidth use kar raha hai, use chuno.
  • IP hash — client IP ka hash karke server chuno. Isse ek hi user hamesha ek hi server par jata hai — session stickiness ke liye useful.

Implementation ke tareeke

  • Smart clients — client khud decide kare kaun se server se baat karni hai (service discovery ke saath).
  • Hardware load balancers — dedicated machines, bahut tez, lekin mehange aur kam flexible.
  • Software load balancers — Nginx, HAProxy jaise tools. Aaj zyada tar systems yehi use karte hain — saste, flexible aur configure karne me aasan.
Interview tip: L4 vs L7 ka farq zaroor batao — L4 (transport layer) sirf IP/port dekh kar baantta hai, L7 (application layer) HTTP headers, URL aur cookies dekh kar smart routing kar sakta hai (jaise /images wale requests image servers par).
SOURCESource: basics/load-balancing.md
04Basics

Caching

Caching ka ek hi principle hai — locality of reference: jo data abhi manga gaya hai, wo dobara manga jane ki probability zyada hai. Cache architecture ke har level par ho sakta hai, lekin aksar front end ke sabse kareeb hota hai.

Application server cache

Cache request layer node par rakha jata hai. Jab request layer ko bahut saare nodes me badhaya jata hai to problem aati hai: load balancer requests ko randomly baantta hai, ek hi request alag-alag nodes par ja sakti hai, aur cache misses badh jate hain. Solutions: global cache ya distributed cache.

Distributed cache

Har request layer node cached data ka ek hissa rakhta hai. Poora cache consistent hashing function se baanta jata hai.

  • Pro — request pool me nodes jod kar cache space aasani se badha sakte ho.
  • Con — ek node gayab ho to uska cache kho jata hai.

Global cache

Ek server ya file store jo original store se tez ho aur saare request layer nodes se accessible ho. Do common forms:

  • Cache server handles cache miss — zyada tar applications yehi karti hain; miss hone par cache server khud database se laata hai.
  • Request nodes handle cache miss — hot data ka bada hissa nodes ke paas hota hai; ye tab jab cached files static hon aur evict nahi honi chahiye, aur application ko eviction strategy ya hot spots ki cache se behtar samajh ho.

Content Distribution Network (CDN)

Static media (images, videos, files) serve karne wali sites ke liye. Process:

  1. Request pehle CDN se static media maangti hai.
  2. CDN ke paas hai to wahi se serve kar deta hai.
  3. Nahi hai to back-end servers se file lekar locally cache karta hai aur user ko serve karta hai.

System chhota ho to CDN ke bina bhi shuru kar sakte ho: static media ko alag subdomain se lightweight HTTP server (jaise Nginx) se serve karo, baad me us subdomain ka DNS CDN par cutover kar do.

Cache invalidation — Source of truth se sync

Cache ko source of truth ke saath coherent rakhna hai. Jab source of truth badle, cache invalidate karo.

StrategyKaise kaam karta haiProCon
Write-throughData cache aur permanent storage me ek saath likha jata haiFast retrieval, poori consistency, disruption se robustWrite operations me zyada latency
Write-aroundData sirf permanent storage me likha jata hai, cache me nahiBekaar cache kam bharte hainAbhi likha data maangne par cache miss + zyada latency
Write-backData sirf cache me likha jata hai, permanent storage me baad meLow latency, write-heavy apps me high throughputSystem disruption par data loss ka risk

Cache eviction policies

  • FIFO — first in, first out (jo pehle aaya wo pehle niklega)
  • LIFO — last in, first out
  • LRU — least recently used (sabse purana use hua data nikalo) — sabse common
  • MRU — most recently used
  • LFU — least frequently used (sabse kam baar use hua data nikalo)
  • RR — random replacement
Interview me aur: cache-aside (application pehle cache dekhti hai, miss par DB se laakar cache bhar deti hai), TTL (time-to-live), cache stampede / thundering herd (ek hi hot key expire hote hi hazaaron requests DB par girna — isse request coalescing ya staggered TTL se rokte hain) — ye terms bhi aani chahiye.
SOURCESource: basics/caching.md
05Basics

Sharding / Data Partitioning

Jab ek database machine par data ya load nahi samaata, to data ko multiple machines (shards) me baantna sharding hai. Har shard data ka ek hissa rakhta hai, aur saare shards mil kar poora dataset banate hain.

Partitioning methods

  • Horizontal partitioning (range based) — alag rows ko alag tables me rakho, range ke hisaab se. Con: agar range wali value carefully nahi chuni, to servers unbalanced ho jayenge (ek shard par saara load).
  • Vertical partitioning — ek feature ka data apne server par. Pro: implement karna straightforward hai, application par low impact. Con: application grow kare to database ko aur partition karna pad sakta hai.
  • Directory-based partitioning — ek lookup service jo partitioning scheme jaanta hai aur use database access code se chhupata hai. DB servers jodna ya scheme badalna application ko affect kiye bina ho jata hai. Con: ye lookup service khud single point of failure ban sakti hai.

Partitioning criteria

  • Key / hash-based — entry ki key attribute par hash function lagakar partition number nikalo. Problem: naye servers jodne par hash function badalna pad sakta hai, jisse data redistribute karna padega aur downtime hoga. Workaround: consistent hashing.
  • List partitioning — har partition ko values ki ek list assign karo (jaise region ke hisaab se: US-East, EU-West).
  • Round-robin partitioning — n partitions hon to i-th tuple partition i % n me jata hai. Simple hai lekin range queries mushkil ho jati hain.
  • Composite partitioning — upar wale schemes ko combine karke naya scheme banao. Consistent hashing hash + list partitioning ka composite hai: key → hash se reduced key space → list → partition.

Common problems of sharding

Zyada tar constraints is wajah se hain ki multiple tables ya ek hi table ki multiple rows par operations ab ek hi server par nahi chalenge.

  • Joins aur denormalization — joins efficient nahi rahenge kyunki data multiple servers se compile karna padega. Workaround: database ko denormalize karo taaki queries ek hi table se ho sakein — lekin isse data inconsistency aa sakti hai.
  • Referential integrity — foreign keys jaise constraints enforce karna mushkil. Workaround: application code se integrity enforce karo, ya SQL jobs chalakar dangling references saaf karo.
  • Rebalancing — data distribution uniform nahi hai ya ek shard par bahut load hai, to aur shards banao ya existing shards rebalance karo — isme partitioning scheme badalna aur data move karna padta hai.
SOURCESource: basics/sharding.md
06Basics

Indexes

Index database me ek aisi structure hai jo search queries ko tez karti hai — bilkul kitab ke peeche wale index ki tarah, jahan se topic ka page number turant mil jata hai.

Repo me kya hai — aur interview me kya aur chahiye

Repo ke indexes wale page par sirf 2 points hain, lekin interview me is topic par bahut poochha jata hai:

  • Search queries ki performance badhti hai — index ke bina database ko poori table scan karni padti hai (full table scan); index ke saath wo seedha sahi rows par ja sakta hai.
  • Write performance kam hoti hai — har insert, update aur delete par index bhi update karna padta hai, isliye writes slow ho jate hain.
Repo note: Repo ke is page par sirf ye 2 points hain. Neeche interview-standard detail diya gaya hai — ye repo ka text nahi hai, lekin interview me isi level ki samajh chahiye.

Index kaise kaam karta hai

  • B-Tree index (default) — zyada tar databases (Postgres, MySQL) B-Tree use karti hain. Range queries (jaise age BETWEEN 20 AND 30) aur sorting ke liye best hai.
  • Hash index — sirf exact match (WHERE id = 5) ke liye bahut tez, lekin range queries nahi kar sakta.
  • Clustered vs non-clustered — clustered index me table ka data khud index ke order me store hota hai (ek table me sirf ek clustered index); non-clustered me index alag structure hai jo row ka pointer rakhta hai.
  • Covering index — agar query ke saare columns index me hi hain, to database ko table touch hi nahi karna padta — sabse tez query.
  • Composite index — multiple columns par ek index; column ka order matter karta hai (leftmost prefix rule).

Trade-off — Kab index lagayein, kab nahi

  • Read-heavy tables par indexes lagao; write-heavy tables par har extra index write ko slow karta hai.
  • WHERE clause, JOIN condition aur ORDER BY me use hone wale columns par index banao.
  • Har column par index mat lagao — har index disk space khata hai aur har write par update hota hai.
  • Low-cardinality columns (jaise gender, true/false) par index kaam ka nahi hota.
SOURCESource: basics/indexes.md
07Basics

Proxies

Proxy server client aur backend server ke beech baitha intermediary hai — hardware ya software ka ek tukda jo requests ko aage badhane se pehle kuch kaam kar sakta hai.

Proxy kya-kya karta hai

  • Filter requests — galat ya harmful requests ko backend tak pahunchne se pehle roko.
  • Log requests — har request ka record rakho (debugging aur analytics ke liye).
  • Transform requests — encryption, compression jaise transformations lagao.
  • Cache — responses cache karke backend ka load kam karo.
  • Batch requests — multiple requests ko ek me milakar backend par bhejo:
    • Collapsed forwarding — ek hi URI ke liye multiple client requests ko backend par ek hi request ki tarah process karo.
    • Spatial batching — storage me paas-paas pada data ek saath maango taaki reads kam hon.
Repo note: Repo ke is page par sirf upar wali list hai. Neeche interview-standard detail hai.

Forward proxy vs Reverse proxy

Forward ProxyReverse Proxy
Kiske saamneClient ke saamne (client ki taraf se)Server ke saamne (server ki taraf se)
KaamClient ki identity chhupana, content filtering, geo-restriction bypassLoad balancing, SSL termination, caching, rate limiting
ExampleOffice/school ka internet filterNginx, Cloudflare, API gateway

System design interviews me jab "proxy" bola jata hai, to zyada tar reverse proxy ki baat hoti hai — Nginx load balancer ke roop me, SSL termination, static files serve karna, aur backend servers ko duniya se chhupana.

API Gateway — Proxy ka bada bhai

Microservices me reverse proxy ko API gateway kehte hain: ek hi entry point jo authentication, rate limiting, request routing, aur response transformation karta hai. Har microservice ke peeche alag proxy lagane se behtar hai ek gateway rakhna.

SOURCESource: basics/proxies.md
08Basics

Queues

Queue ek asynchronous buffer hai — client ki request aur us request par hone wale asal kaam ke beech ka abstraction. Client task submit karke turant aage badh sakta hai; kaam peeche se hota rehta hai.

Queue kyun chahiye

  • Asynchronous communication — system ke alag components ko ek dusre ka wait kiye bina kaam karne do. Client task submit kare, result ka wait na kare.
  • Decoupling — producer (request bhejne wala) aur consumer (kaam karne wala) ek dusre ko jaane bina kaam karte hain; consumer ko badla ya scale kiya ja sakta hai.
  • Outage se protection — agar backend service down hai ya slow hai, to requests queue me safe rehti hain; service wapas aate hi process ho jati hain.
  • Load smoothing — achanak traffic spike aaye to queue use absorb kar leti hai; consumers apni speed se kaam karte hain (backpressure).
Repo note: Repo ke is page par sirf 4 points hain. Neeche interview-standard detail hai.

Queue ke patterns

  • Point-to-point — ek message ek hi consumer ko milta hai (jaise job queue: email bhejna, image resize karna).
  • Publish-subscribe (pub-sub) — ek message multiple subscribers ko milta hai (jaise nayi post aane par notification service, search indexer aur analytics teeno ko khabar).
  • Dead-letter queue (DLQ) — jo messages baar-baar fail hon, unhe alag queue me daalo taaki wo main queue ko block na karein aur baad me debug ho sakein.
  • Delayed / scheduled queue — message ko kuch time baad deliver karo (jaise 24 ghante baad reminder email).

Real examples

  • Kafka — high-throughput event streaming; messages ko topics me baant ta hai, multiple consumers parallel me padhte hain.
  • RabbitMQ / SQS — classic message queues; task distribution aur decoupling ke liye.
  • Redis Streams / Lists — halki-phulki queue jab alag infrastructure nahi chahiye.

Interview me: jab bhi system me "user ko turant jawab chahiye lekin kaam slow hai" (email, notification, video processing, report generation) — queue ka naam lo. Aur poochho: message ordering chahiye? Exactly-once delivery chahiye? (Aksar at-least-once hi milta hai — idempotency se handle karte hain.)

SOURCESource: basics/queues.md
09Basics

Redundancy

Redundancy matlab critical data ya services ki duplication — taaki ek cheez fail ho to dusri sambhal le aur system ki reliability badhe.

Server failover

Single points of failure hatao aur backups rakho. Ek server down ho to dusra (standby) turant uski jagah le le — ise failover kehte hain. Failover do tarah ka hota hai:

  • Active-passive — ek server kaam karta hai, dusra standby rehta hai; fail hone par standby active ho jata hai.
  • Active-active — dono servers kaam karte hain aur load baant te hain; ek fail ho to dusra poora load sambhal leta hai.

Shared-nothing architecture

  • Har node ek dusre se independently operate kar sakta hai.
  • State manage karne ya activities orchestrate karne wali koi central service nahi hoti.
  • Naye servers bina kisi special condition ya knowledge ke jode ja sakte hain.
  • Koi single point of failure nahi hota.
Repo note: Repo ke is page par sirf upar wale points hain. Neeche interview-standard detail hai.

Data redundancy — Replication

Data ki bhi redundancy hoti hai: ek hi data ki multiple copies alag machines (ya alag data centers) par rakho — ise replication kehte hain.

  • Primary-replica — writes primary par, reads replicas se. Primary fail ho to replica primary ban jata hai.
  • Multi-primary — har node write kar sakta hai; conflicts ko resolve karna padta hai.
  • Quorum — write/read tabhi success jab N nodes me se W/R nodes maan jayein (jaise Dynamo/Cassandra).

RTO aur RPO — Do terms jo interviewer sunna chahta hai

  • RTO (Recovery Time Objective) — fail hone ke baad system kitni der me wapas chalna chahiye.
  • RPO (Recovery Point Objective) — kitna data loss acceptable hai (jaise 5 minute ka data kho sakta hai, 1 ghante ka nahi).

Dono ka jawab budget tay karta hai: zero data loss aur zero downtime chahiye to cost bahut zyada hogi. Interview me hamesha trade-off batao.

SOURCESource: basics/redundancy.md
10Basics

SQL vs NoSQL

Database chunna system design ke sabse pehle decisions me se ek hai. SQL aur NoSQL alag problems ke liye bane hain — dono ko samajhna zaroori hai, ek ko "behtar" kehna galat hai.

NoSQL ke common types

  • Key-value stores — key-value pairs ka array. "Key" ek attribute name hota hai. Examples: Redis, Voldemort, Dynamo.
  • Document databases — data documents me store hota hai; documents collections me group hote hain; har document ki structure bilkul alag ho sakti hai. Examples: CouchDB, MongoDB.
  • Wide-column / columnar databases — column families (rows ke containers). Saare columns pehle se jaanna zaroori nahi; har row me alag number of columns ho sakte hain. Examples: Cassandra, HBase.
  • Graph databases — data graph structures me store hota hai: nodes (entities), properties (entities ki information), lines (connections). Examples: Neo4j, InfiniteGraph.

SQL vs NoSQL — Differences

AspectSQLNoSQL
StorageData tables me store hota haiAlag-alag data storage models
SchemaHar record fixed schema follow karta hai; schema badalna poori database modify karna haiSchemas dynamic hote hain
QueryingSQL (structured query language) se define aur manipulate karte hainQueries ek collection of documents par focused hoti hain; alag databases ki alag syntax (UnQL — unstructured query language)
ScalabilityVertically scalable (horsepower badhao: memory, CPU) — mehenga; horizontally bhi ho sakta hai lekin challenging aur time-consumingHorizontally scalable (servers jodo) — sasta
ACIDACID compliant — data reliability, transactions ki guaranteeZyada tar performance aur scalability ke liye ACID compliance sacrifice karte hain

ACID = Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.

Kaun sa kab use karein

  • SQL chuno jab: ACID compliance chahiye (anomalies kam karo, database integrity protect karo); data structured hai aur badalta nahi hai.
  • NoSQL chuno jab: data ki structure kam hai ya bilkul nahi hai; cloud computing aur storage ka poora fayda lena hai (cloud-based storage ke liye data ko multiple servers par spread karna aasan hona chahiye); rapid development hai aur data structure frequently update hota hai.
Interview tip: "SQL vs NoSQL" ka jawab kabhi ek line me mat do. Data model, query patterns, consistency needs aur scale — chaaro pe baat karo. Aur yaad rakho: aaj ke real systems dono use karte hain (jaise Postgres + Redis + Elasticsearch ek hi system me).
SOURCESource: basics/sql-vs-nosql.md
11Basics

CAP Theorem

CAP theorem distributed systems ka sabse zyada galat samjha jaane wala concept hai — aur interview me sabse zyada poochha jaane wala bhi. Ise sahi samajh lo to aadhi design discussions aasan ho jati hain.

Teen guarantees

  • Consistency — har read ko sabse recent write mile, ya error mile.
  • Availability — har request ko response mile jo error na ho.
  • Partition tolerance — nodes ke beech network messages drop ya delay hone par bhi system chalta rahe.

Theorem kya kehta hai

CAP theorem kehta hai: network partition hone par consistency aur availability me se ek ko chunna padega. Dono ek saath nahi mil sakte — kyunki partition ke do hisse ek dusre se baat nahi kar sakte, to ya to purana data do (available raho, consistency chhodo) ya jawab hi mat do (consistent raho, availability chhodo).

Sabse badi galatfahmi: CAP ka matlab ye nahi hai ki hamesha teen me se ek guarantee chhodni padegi. Asliyat me, chunav sirf tab hota hai jab network partition ya failure ho; baaki saare time koi trade-off nahi karna padta. Partition ke bina C aur A dono mil sakte hain.

ACID vs BASE

  • ACID databases consistency ko availability par prefer karti hain (jaise traditional relational databases).
  • BASE systems availability ko consistency par prefer karte hain aur eventual consistency accept karte hain (jaise bahut saari NoSQL systems).

Interview examples

  • CP chuno (Consistency + Partition tolerance): banking, payments — galat balance dikhana ek second ke liye bhi acceptable nahi hai; system thoda down rahe to chalega.
  • AP chuno (Availability + Partition tolerance): shopping cart, social feed — thoda purana data dikh jaye to chalega, lekin site down nahi honi chahiye.
  • Partition tolerance distributed system me practically hamesha chahiye hoti hai — network kabhi na kabhi fail hoga hi. Isliye asli choice C aur A ke beech hoti hai.
SOURCESource: basics/cap-theorem.md
12Basics

Consistent Hashing

Consistent hashing wo technique hai jo distributed cache aur sharded databases ko server jodne/hatane par tootne se bachati hai. Simple hashing me ek server badla to saara mapping bikhar jata hai — consistent hashing me sirf k/n keys remap hoti hain.

Simple hashing ki problems — key % n

Key ko server number se map karna: server = hash(key) % n (n = servers ki sankhya). Do badi problems:

  • Horizontally scalable nahi hai — jab bhi naya cache host jodo, saare existing mappings toot jate hain (kyunki n badal gaya, to har key ka % n badal gaya).
  • Load balanced nahi hai — khaas taur par non-uniform data ke liye; kuch servers hot spots ban jate hain (un par zyada load).

Consistent hashing kaise kaam karta hai

  • Consistent hashing ek key ko ek integer me map karta hai.
  • Imagine karo integers ki range ek ring par rakhi hai — values wrap around hoti hain (jaise ghadi).
  • Servers ki list ko bhi hash karke integers me map karo aur ring par rakho.
  • Key ko server map karne ke liye: key ko ek integer me hash karo, phir ring par clockwise chalo jab tak pehla cache (server) na mile — wahi server us key ka owner hai.
  • Jab hash table resize ho (server add ya delete ho), to sirf k/n keys remap karni padti hain (k = total keys, n = servers ki sankhya). Baaki keys wahi rehti hain.

Hot spots — Virtual replicas

Hot spots handle karne ke liye caches ke "virtual replicas" banao:

  • Har cache ko ring par ek point ki jagah multiple points par map karo (replicas). Isse har cache ring ke multiple portions se jud jata hai.
  • Agar hash function achha "mix" karta hai, to replicas ki sankhya badhne par keys zyada balanced ho jati hain.
Example: 4 servers, 1,000,000 keys. Ek server jodo (n=4 → 5): simple hashing me ~1,000,000 keys remap hoti hain (lagbhag saari). Consistent hashing me sirf ~200,000 (k/n = 1,000,000/5) keys move hoti hain. Interview me ye number zaroor batao — isi liye consistent hashing use hoti hai.

Kahan use hoti hai: distributed caches (Memcached, Redis Cluster), sharded databases (Cassandra, DynamoDB), CDNs, load balancers. Lab 1 me ring ko khud chala kar dekho.

SOURCESource: basics/consistent-hashing.md
13Basics

Client-Server Communication

Client aur server ke beech data kaise aata-jata hai — ye choice har real-time feature (chat, live feed, notifications) ki neev hai. 5 patterns hain, aur har ek ke trade-offs alag hain.

Standard HTTP Web Request

  1. Client connection kholta hai aur server se data maangta hai.
  2. Server response calculate karta hai.
  3. Server khule hue request par response bhej deta hai.

Simple hai, lekin har baar naya connection aur naya request chahiye — real-time updates ke liye nahi bana.

Ajax Polling

Client baar-baar server se data maangta hai aur response ka wait karta hai. Data na ho to empty response milta hai.

  1. Client regular HTTP se connection khol kar data maangta hai.
  2. Webpage regular intervals par (jaise 0.5 seconds) server ko requests bhejti hai.
  3. Server response calculate karke bhejta hai, normal HTTP traffic ki tarah.
  4. Client updates paane ke liye upar wale 3 steps periodically repeat karta hai.

Problems: client ko naye data ke liye baar-baar poochhna padta hai; bahut saare responses empty hote hain — HTTP overhead banta hai.

HTTP Long-Polling

Client normal polling ki tarah information maangta hai, lekin is expectation ke saath ki server turant respond nahi karega.

  1. Client regular HTTP se initial request karta hai aur response ka wait karta hai.
  2. Server response delay karta hai jab tak update available na ho ya timeout na ho jaye.
  3. Update aate hi server poora response bhej deta hai.
  4. Client turant naya long-poll request bhejta hai (response milte hi ya acceptable latency ke liye pause ke baad).

Har long-poll request ka timeout hota hai. Timeout ke baad connection band ho jata hai, to client ko periodically reconnect karna padta hai.

WebSockets

  • Ek hi TCP connection par persistent full-duplex communication channel — server aur client dono kisi bhi time data bhej sakte hain.
  • Connection WebSocket handshake se establish hota hai.
  • Low communication overhead aur real-time data transfer.

Chat apps, live collaboration, multiplayer games — jahan dono taraf se turant data chahiye, wahan WebSockets best hai.

Server-Sent Events (SSE)

  1. Client regular HTTP se server se data maangta hai.
  2. Webpage ek connection kholti hai.
  3. Server jab bhi nayi information hoti hai, data bhej deta hai.

Use case: jab server se client ki taraf real-time traffic chahiye ho; jab server ek loop me data generate karke multiple events bheje (jaise live score, stock ticker, log stream).

PatternDirectionOverheadKab use karein
HTTP requestClient → ServerHar request par nayaNormal API calls
PollingClient → ServerZyada (empty responses)Simple, kam-frequent updates
Long-pollingServer → ClientMediumUpdates kabhi-kabhi aayein
WebSocketsDono tarafKamChat, gaming, collaboration
SSEServer → ClientKamLive feed, notifications
SOURCESource: basics/client-server-communication.md
14System Designs

Short URL Service

URL shortening service (jaise bit.ly) — lambi URL ko chhota, unique alias do, aur short link kholne par original URL par redirect karo. Ye repo ka ekmatra poora likha hua design hai — requirements, capacity estimation, APIs, database schema aur algorithms sab kuch.

Requirements

Functional Requirements

  • URL di jaye to uska shorter aur unique alias (short link) generate karo.
  • User short link khole to original link par redirect karo.
  • User optionally apni URL ke liye custom short link pick kar sake.
  • Links ek standard default timespan ke baad expire ho jayein; user expiration time specify bhi kar sake.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • System highly available hona chahiye — service down hui to saari URL redirections fail hone lagengi.
  • URL redirection real-time me minimal latency ke saath honi chahiye.
  • Shortened links guessable (predictable) nahi hone chahiye.

Extended Requirements

  • Analytics — kitni baar redirection hua?
  • Doosri services ke liye REST APIs se accessible ho.

Capacity Estimation and Constraints

Assumption: read-heavy system hai — naye URL shorten karne se zyada redirection requests hongi. Read aur write ka ratio 100:1 maano.

Traffic estimates

  • 500M naye URL shortenings per month → 100 × 500M = 50B redirections per month.
  • Naye URL shortenings per second: 500 million / (30 days × 24 hours × 3600 seconds) = ~200 URLs/s.
  • URL redirections per second: 50 billion / (30 days × 24 hours × 3600 sec) = ~19K/s.

Storage estimates

  • Har URL shortening request ko 5 saal tak store karo, har object 500 bytes.
  • Total objects: 500 million × 5 years × 12 months = 30 billion.
  • Total storage: 30 billion × 500 bytes = 15 TB.

Bandwidth estimates

  • Write: 200 URL/s × 500 bytes/URL = 100 KB/s.
  • Read: 19K URL/s × 500 bytes/URL = ~9 MB/s.

Cache memory estimates

  • 80-20 rule follow karo: 20% URLs 80% traffic generate karti hain, to 20% hot URLs cache karo.
  • Requests per day: 19K × 3600 seconds × 24 hours = ~1.7 billion/day.
  • Cache 20%: 0.2 × 1.7 billion × 500 bytes = ~170 GB.
CategoryCalculationEstimate
New URLs500 million / (30 days × 24 hours × 3600 seconds)200 /s
URL redirections500 million × 100 / (30 days × 24 hours × 3600 seconds)19 K/s
Incoming data500 bytes/URL × 200 URL/s100 KB/s
Outgoing data500 bytes/URL × 19K URL/s9 MB/s
Storage for 5 years500 bytes/URL × 500 million × 60 months15 TB
Memory for cache19K URL × 3600 seconds × 24 hours × 500 bytes × 20%170 GB

System APIs

createUrl

ParameterTypeNote
api_dev_keystringRegistered account ki API developer key — isse users ko unke allocated quota ke hisaab se throttle karte hain
original_urlstringOriginal URL jo shorten karni hai
custom_aliasstringOptional custom key for the URL
user_namestringOptional user name jo encoding me use hoga
expire_datestringOptional expiration date for the shortened URL

Return: string — successful insertion par shortened URL return hoti hai, warna error code.

deleteUrl

ParameterTypeNote
api_dev_keystringRegistered account ki API developer key — quota ke hisaab se throttle karne ke liye
url_keystringShort URL

Return: string — successful deletion par 'URL Removed' return hota hai.

Database design

Observations

  • Billions of records store karne hain.
  • Har object chhota hai (1K se kam).
  • Records ke beech koi relationship nahi hai — sirf ye store karna hai ki kis user ne URL banayi.
  • Read-heavy system hai.
  • NoSQL choice scale karna aasan banayega. (Comment: sharding ke saath SQL bhi kaam karega.)

Schema — URL table

ColumnType
hashvarchar(16)
original_urlvarchar(512)
creation_datedatetime
expiration_datedatetime
user_idint

Schema — User table

ColumnType
namevarchar(20)
emailvarchar(32)
creation_datedatetime
last_logindatetime

Basic System Design and Algorithm — Encoding actual URL

Unique hash compute karo

  • base64 alphabet: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, -, . — total 64 characters.
  • 6 letters: 64 ^ 6 = ~68.7 billion unique keys.
  • 8 letters: 64 ^ 8 = ~281 trillion unique keys.
  • 6 letters use karo — 68.7 billion hamari 30 billion URLs ke liye kaafi hai.
  • MD5 128-bit hash value generate karta hai; har base64 character 6 bits encode karta hai, to base64 encoding 22 characters deti hai — unme se 8 characters select karo.

Is approach ki issues

  • Multiple users se same URL aaye to kya hoga?
  • URL-encoded input kaise handle karein?

Workaround — input URL me ek increasing sequence number append karo aur uska hash generate karo; ya user id append karo.

Generating keys offline — Key Generation Service (KGS)

  • Standalone Key Generation Service: random 6-letter strings generate karke database (key DB) me store karo. Jab short URL chahiye ho, key DB se ek key le lo.
  • Key DB size: 6 characters/key × 68.7B unique keys = 412 GB.
  • Concurrency issue: agar multiple servers concurrently keys padh rahe hon, to do ya zyada servers ek hi key padhne ki koshish kar sakte hain.
  • Workaround: servers KGS use karke keys ko database me read/mark karein. KGS do tables use kar sakta hai — ek unused keys ke liye, ek saari used keys ke liye. KGS hamesha kuch keys memory me rakhe taaki jab bhi server ko chahiye ho, turant de sake. KGS ko ensure karna hai ki ek hi key multiple servers ko na de. (Comment: keys sharded hain — har KGS server sirf ek application server ko serve karta hai.)

Key lookup: key mili to HTTP 302 Redirect status ke saath stored URL pass karo; key na mile to HTTP 404 Not Found do ya homepage par redirect karo.

UUID: KGS ki jagah UUID bhi use kar sakte ho.

Data Partitioning and Replication

  • Range-based partitioning — URLs ko URL ya hash key ke pehle letter ke hisaab se alag partitions me store karo; kam frequently aane wale letters ko ek hi database partition me combine karo. Problem: unbalanced servers.
  • Hash-based partitioning — short URL ka hash lekar uske hisaab se partition calculate karo. Consistent hashing use karo.

Cache

  • Eviction policy: LRU — least recently used URL pehle discard karo.
  • Cache update: cache miss par backend database se lao aur nayi entry saare cache replicas ko do.

Load Balancer

LB locations:

  • Clients aur application servers ke beech.
  • Application servers aur database servers ke beech.
  • Application servers aur cache servers ke beech.

DB Sweeping, Telemetry, Security

  • DB Sweeping: ek alag Cleanup service periodically chal kar expired links ko storage aur cache se remove kare.
  • Telemetry: system ke statistics — ek short URL kitni baar use hui.
  • Security and Permissions: har URL ke saath permission level (public/private) store karo; unauthorized access par error (HTTP 401) bhejo.
SOURCESource: designs/short-url.md
15System Designs

Pastebin

Pastebin — text snippets (code, logs, notes) share karne ki service. User text paste karta hai, ek short link milta hai, aur link kholne wala wahi text padh sakta hai. Kuch pastes public hote hain, kuch private, kuch expiry ke saath.

Repo note: Repo ki Pastebin wali file me sirf 2 diagrams hain (overview + detail) — koi likha hua design nahi hai. Neeche wahi diagrams samjhaye gaye hain, aur har design decision diagram ke components se liya gaya hai.

Requirements

  • Functional: user text paste kare aur unique URL paye; URL kholne par wahi text dikhe; paste public/private ho sakta hai; optional expiry (10 minute se 1 saal tak); optional custom URL; user account se apne pastes manage kare.
  • Non-functional: high availability aur reliability (paste kho jaye to user ka data gaya); low latency reads; scale: millions of pastes per day.

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview diagram me flow seedha hai: Client → Load Balancer → Application Servers → Metadata Store + Object Storage. Text content (jo bada ho sakta hai) object storage me jata hai (jaise S3), aur uska metadata — paste ID, owner, expiry, visibility — database me rehta hai. Read path par app server pehle metadata dekhta hai (expiry/permission check), phir object storage se content laata hai.

Diagram walkthrough — Detailed design

Detail diagram me do flows alag dikhte hain:

  • Write flow: paste submit → app server unique key generate karta hai (Short URL wale KGS jaisa) → metadata DB me entry + content object storage me → short URL return.
  • Read flow: short URL → metadata lookup (cache me pehle dekho — hot pastes ke liye) → expiry/permission check → object storage se content → response.

Data model

FieldType / Note
paste_id / keyShort unique key (6-8 chars, base62)
content_urlObject storage ka path
user_idOptional — anonymous pastes bhi hote hain
created_at, expires_atExpiry ke liye
visibilitypublic / unlisted / private

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Read-heavy: popular pastes ko cache karo (metadata + content dono); CDN se static content serve karo.
  • Storage: content object storage me (cheap, unlimited); metadata relational ya NoSQL DB me — paste_id par partition karo.
  • Expiry: cleanup service periodically expired pastes hataye (Short URL wali DB sweeping jaisi).
  • Bottleneck: agar ek paste viral ho jaye to uske liye cache stampede — hot key ko cache me rakho aur read replicas badhao.
SOURCESource: designs/pastebin.md
16System Designs

Instagram

Instagram — photo/video sharing: users media upload karte hain, follow karte hain, aur home feed me un logon ki posts dekhte hain jinhe wo follow karte hain. Scale ka sawaal hai: billions of photos aur feed generation.

Repo note: Repo ki Instagram wali file me sirf 2 diagrams hain (overview + detail). Neeche wahi diagrams samjhaye gaye hain.

Requirements

  • Functional: photo/video upload (multiple sizes — thumbnails bhi), follow/unfollow, home feed (follow kiye gaye logon ki posts, latest pehle), like/comment, user profile page.
  • Non-functional: high availability; feed load karna fast hona chahiye (user 2 second se zyada wait nahi karta); photos reliably store honi chahiye (kabhi khoyengi nahi); massive scale — millions of uploads per day.

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me 3 bade hisse dikhte hain: upload flow (client → LB → app servers → object storage), feed flow (feed service → cache → client), aur storage (media files object storage me, metadata database me). Photo upload hote hi multiple sizes generate hote hain (thumbnail, medium, full) — ye kaam async workers karte hain, upload request ka wait nahi karwate.

Diagram walkthrough — Detailed design

Detail diagram me feed generation ka design hai:

  • Fanout on write (push): jab celebrity post karta hai, to uski post uske saare followers ke feed me pehle se daal di jati hai — read time par feed banana nahi padta. Feed read karna ek cache lookup ban jata hai.
  • Fanout on read (pull): normal users ke liye feed read time par banayi jati hai — follow list se recent posts lao aur merge karo.
  • Hybrid: celebrities ke liye pull, normal users ke liye push — kyunki celebrity ke millions of followers hain, unke liye push bahut mehenga padega.
  • Media storage: photos object storage (S3 jaisi) me, CDN se serve hoti hain — user ke kareeb ke edge se photo aati hai.

Data model

EntityFields
Useruser_id, username, profile, followers/following counts
Photophoto_id, user_id, storage URLs (multiple sizes), caption, created_at
Followfollower_id, followee_id (graph ya relational table)
Feeduser_id → photo_ids ki list (cache me, time-ordered)

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Feed generation sabse bada bottleneck hai — fanout strategy (push/pull/hybrid) se solve karo.
  • Storage: photos kabhi delete nahi hoti — object storage + CDN, aur thumbnails alag se.
  • Hot users: celebrity posts par like/comment ka storm — counters ko sharded counters ya async aggregation se handle karo.
  • Consistency: feed me thodi eventual consistency chalegi — nayi post 1-2 second der se dikhe to koi problem nahi.
SOURCESource: designs/instagram.md
17System Designs

Dropbox

Dropbox — file sync aur storage: user kisi bhi device se file daale, wo har device par sync ho jaye. Challenge: badi files ko efficiently sync karna, conflicts handle karna, aur storage cost kam rakhna.

Repo note: Repo ki Dropbox wali file me sirf 2 diagrams hain (overview + detail). Neeche wahi diagrams samjhaye gaye hain.

Requirements

  • Functional: files upload/download karo; kisi bhi device se access; files share karo (link ya collaborators); file versions rakho; offline changes baad me sync hon.
  • Non-functional: high reliability (data kabhi khoye nahi); fast sync (chhota change turant sync ho); huge scale (billions of files); storage efficient.

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me client ke beech me sync service hai, uske peeche metadata database (file ka naam, size, version, permissions) aur block storage (file ka asal content). Client seedha block storage se baat nahi karta — metadata service batati hai kaun sa block kahan hai.

Diagram walkthrough — Detailed design

Detail diagram ki khaas baatein:

  • Chunking: badi file ko chhote blocks (jaise 4MB) me todo. Sirf badla hua block dobara upload hota hai — poori file nahi. Isse bandwidth aur time dono bachte hain.
  • Content hash: har block ka hash rakho — agar do users ke paas same block hai, to ek hi copy store karo (deduplication).
  • Sync flow: client file change karta hai → sirf changed blocks upload → metadata update → doosre devices ko notification (long-polling ya push) → wo devices sirf naye blocks download karte hain.
  • Conflict handling: ek hi file do jagah badli to dono versions rakho aur user ko batayo (conflicted copy) — silent overwrite kabhi mat karo.

Data model

EntityFields
File metadatafile_id, user_id, path, size, version, modified_at
Blockblock_hash, size, storage location
File → Blocksfile_id → ordered list of block hashes

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Storage cost: deduplication + compression se kam karo; cold files ko saste storage par rakho.
  • Sync traffic: chunking se sirf delta sync hota hai — poori file dobara nahi jati.
  • Metadata: billions of files ka metadata — sharded database, file_id par partition.
  • Notifications: millions of devices ko real-time batana hai — push service + long-polling ka combo.
SOURCESource: designs/dropbox.md
18System Designs

Twitter

Twitter — short messages (tweets): user tweet karta hai, followers ke timeline me dikhta hai, aur search se purane tweets milte hain. Sabse bada challenge: celebrity ke tweet par fanout aur timeline generation.

Repo note: Repo ki Twitter wali file me sirf 2 diagrams hain (overview + detail). Neeche wahi diagrams samjhaye gaye hain.

Requirements

  • Functional: tweet post karo (280 chars), timeline dekho (follow kiye gaye logon ke tweets), like/retweet/reply, user search aur tweet search, trending topics.
  • Non-functional: timeline load fast hona chahiye; tweet post karte hi followers ko dikhna chahiye (seconds me); massive scale — hundreds of millions of users, billions of tweets.

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me: client → LB → app servers → timeline service → cache + tweet store. Tweet likhne par wo tweet store me jata hai; timeline padhne par timeline service cache se pre-computed timeline deti hai.

Diagram walkthrough — Detailed design

  • Fanout on write: normal user tweet kare to uske followers ke timelines me tweet push kar do — timeline read ek cache lookup ban jata hai.
  • Celebrity problem: millions of followers wale user ke liye fanout bahut mehenga hai — iske liye fanout on read use karo (celebrity ke tweets timeline read karte time merge karo) ya fanout ko async workers se dheere-dheere karo.
  • Timeline storage: har user ki timeline (tweet IDs ki list) cache me rakho (Redis jaisi), time-ordered. Purane tweets ke liye database se lao.
  • Search: tweets ko search index me daalo (inverted index) — Twitter Search wale section me detail hai.

Data model

EntityFields
Tweettweet_id, user_id, text, created_at, reply_to, media URLs
Useruser_id, username, followers/following counts
Timelineuser_id → tweet_ids (cache, time-ordered)

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Fanout cost: celebrity tweets — hybrid push/pull se handle karo.
  • Write-heavy spikes: bade events par tweet storm — message queue se writes ko buffer karo.
  • Timeline consistency: thodi eventual consistency acceptable hai — tweet 1-2 second der se dikhe to chalega.
SOURCESource: designs/twitter.md
19System Designs

YouTube

YouTube — video sharing: users video upload karte hain, doosre users dekhte hain, like/comment/subscribe karte hain. Challenge: badi video files ko store karna, har device par chalane layak banana, aur billions of views serve karna.

Repo note: Repo ki YouTube wali file me sirf 2 diagrams hain (overview + detail). Neeche wahi diagrams samjhaye gaye hain.

Requirements

  • Functional: video upload karo; video dekho (multiple resolutions — 144p se 4K tak); search aur recommendations; like/comment/subscribe; channel page.
  • Non-functional: video playback smooth honi chahiye (buffering nahi); upload ke baad video jaldi available ho; storage reliable ho; massive scale — billions of views per day.

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me: client → LB → app servers → video processing + storage + CDN. Upload hote hi video processing pipeline me jati hai, aur playback CDN se hota hai — user ke kareeb wale edge server se.

Diagram walkthrough — Detailed design

  • Upload + transcoding: ek video upload hote hi use multiple resolutions aur formats me convert (transcode) kiya jata hai — ye kaam async workers karte hain, upload request ka wait nahi karwate. Har resolution ke multiple chunks bante hain (adaptive streaming).
  • Adaptive streaming (DASH/HLS): video chhote segments me tooti hoti hai; player network speed ke hisaab se resolution badalta rehta hai — slow network par 144p, tez par 1080p.
  • Storage: original video + saare transcoded versions object storage me; metadata (title, description, views, likes) database me.
  • Delivery: videos CDN se serve hoti hain — popular videos edge par cache rehti hain, isliye playback fast hota hai.
  • Thumbnails: har video ke multiple thumbnails generate hote hain; ek frame ko thumbnail banao ya alag se upload karo.

Data model

EntityFields
Videovideo_id, user_id, title, description, storage URLs (per resolution), views, likes, created_at
User / Channeluser_id, channel name, subscribers count
Commentcomment_id, video_id, user_id, text, created_at

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Transcoding cost: har video ko 5-6 resolutions me convert karna CPU-heavy hai — queue se workers ko distribute karo, popular videos ko priority do.
  • Storage: exabytes ka data — object storage + cold storage for rarely watched videos.
  • Views counter: billions of views — exact count real-time me mat rakho; sharded counters + periodic aggregation.
  • Recommendations: feed me kya dikhana hai — ye ek alag ML system hai; design interview me iska naam lo aur scope se bahar rakho (ya high-level batao).
SOURCESource: designs/youtube.md
20System Designs

Twitter Search

Twitter Search — billions of tweets me se seconds me relevant results dhoondhna. Challenge: data har second badal raha hai (real-time indexing), aur query par ranking bhi karni hai.

Repo note: Repo ki Twitter Search wali file me sirf 2 diagrams hain (overview + detail). Neeche wahi diagrams samjhaye gaye hain.

Requirements

  • Functional: keywords se tweets search karo; users/hashtags search karo; results relevance ke hisaab se rank karo; real-time — abhi post hua tweet search me aana chahiye.
  • Non-functional: query latency low (100ms ke andar); massive scale; search available rahe (down na ho).

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me: query → LB → search service → inverted index → ranked results. Tweet likhte hi wo index me jata hai (write path), aur search karte hi index se results aate hain (read path).

Diagram walkthrough — Detailed design

  • Inverted index: har word → us word wale tweet IDs ki list. Query aate hi words ke lists ko intersect karo (AND) ya union karo (OR). Index sharded hota hai — har shard index ka ek hissa rakhta hai.
  • Real-time indexing: naya tweet aate hi use turant index me daalo (in-memory index pehle, phir disk par flush). Isi liye abhi ka tweet abhi search me milta hai.
  • Ranking: results ko rank karo — recency, engagement (likes/retweets), user authority (verified/followers), aur query se match ki quality.
  • Caching: popular queries (trending hashtags) ke results cache me rakho.
  • Fanout: index ke saare shards se parallel me poochho aur results merge karo (scatter-gather).

Data model

EntityFields
Inverted index entryterm → sorted list of tweet_ids (with positions)
Tweet documenttweet_id, text, user_id, created_at, engagement counts

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Index size: billions of tweets — index ko shards me baanto; har shard apne hisse ka index rakhe.
  • Write throughput: har second hazaaron tweets index karne hain — in-memory index + background flush.
  • Hot terms: trending word ka list bahut badi ho jati hai — us term ke liye top-K results hi rakho ya shard karo.
SOURCESource: designs/twitter-search.md
21System Designs

Web Crawler

Web Crawler — poora internet crawl karke pages download karna (jaise search engine karta hai). Challenge: billions of pages, politeness (ek hi site ko overload mat karo), duplicates, aur badalte hue content ko dobara crawl karna.

Repo note: Repo ki Web Crawler wali file me sirf 2 diagrams hain (overview + detail). Neeche wahi diagrams samjhaye gaye hain.

Requirements

  • Functional: seed URLs se shuru karke links follow karte hue pages crawl karo; page content download aur store karo; naye/updated pages ko dobara crawl karo.
  • Non-functional: polite raho (robots.txt maano, ek host par rate limit rakho); duplicates se bacho; scale — billions of pages; fault-tolerant (ek worker fail ho to crawl rukna nahi chahiye).

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me: URL Frontier (queue) → Fetcher workers → Parser → Storage + naye URLs wapas Frontier me. Ye ek loop hai — crawler kabhi "khatam" nahi hota, naye links milte rehte hain.

Diagram walkthrough — Detailed design

  • URL Frontier: crawl karne wali URLs ki priority queue. Politeness ke liye URLs ko host ke hisaab se alag queues me rakho — ek host ki URLs ek saath fetch mat karo.
  • Fetcher: workers URLs fetch karte hain (HTTP request, timeout, retry). robots.txt check karo pehle — disallowed URLs fetch mat karo.
  • Parser + Link extractor: HTML parse karke naye links nikalo aur frontier me daalo; page content ko index/storage ko bhejo.
  • Deduplication: URL ka hash rakho (pehle crawl ki hai ya nahi); content ka hash rakho (same content alag URL par ho to dobara store mat karo).
  • Re-crawl: pages kitni baar badalte hain, uske hisaab se dobara crawl karo — news sites roz, purani docs kabhi-kabhi.
  • DNS + politeness: DNS results cache karo; ek domain par delay rakho (jaise 1 request/second).

Data model

EntityFields
URL recordurl hash, url, last crawled, crawl frequency, host
Page contentcontent hash, raw HTML / text, fetched_at

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Frontier size: billions of URLs — frontier ko distributed queue me rakho (Kafka jaisi), host-based partitioning ke saath.
  • Network: crawler network-bound hota hai — thousands of parallel fetchers, connection pooling.
  • Politeness vs speed: trade-off hai — tez crawl karo to sites block kar deti hain; isliye per-host rate limiting zaroori hai.
  • Storage: petabytes of HTML — object storage + compression.
SOURCESource: designs/web-crawler.md
22System Designs

Facebook Newsfeed

Facebook Newsfeed — doston ki posts, photos aur updates ka personalized feed. Instagram/Twitter feed jaisa hi problem hai, lekin scale aur ranking zyada complex hai — feed sirf time-ordered nahi hoti, ranking se banti hai.

Repo note: Repo ki Newsfeed wali file me sirf 1 diagram hai (overview) — detail diagram repo me nahi hai. Neeche overview diagram samjhaya gaya hai.

Requirements

  • Functional: post banao (text/photo/video/link); doston ki posts ka feed dekho; like/comment/share karo; feed personalized ho (har user ko alag order).
  • Non-functional: feed load fast ho; post karte hi doston ko dikhe; massive scale — billions of users aur posts.

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me: post creation → fanout service → feed cache → ranking → client. Post bante hi fanout hota hai (friends ke feeds me post ID daal do), aur feed read karte time ranking lagti hai (kis post ko upar dikhana hai).

Feed generation — Push, pull aur ranking

  • Fanout on write (push): post bante hi friends ke feed me daal do — read time par feed banana nahi padta.
  • Ranking: Facebook ka feed time-ordered nahi hai — har post ko score milta hai: tumhara us dost se interaction kitna hai, post kitni fresh hai, post ka type kya hai, kitne logon ne engage kiya. Score ke hisaab se order banta hai.
  • Cache: har user ka feed (post IDs ki ranked list) cache me rakho; post ka content alag se lao (post store / CDN se).
  • Pagination: feed ek saath poori mat lao — pehle 10-20 posts, scroll karne par aur (cursor-based pagination).

Data model

EntityFields
Postpost_id, user_id, content, media URLs, created_at, privacy
Feeduser_id → ranked post_ids (cache)
Friend graphuser_id → friend_ids (graph store)

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Fanout cost: 5000 friends wale user ki post 5000 feeds me jati hai — async workers se fanout karo, post request ka wait mat karwao.
  • Ranking compute: har feed read par ranking karna mehenga hai — pre-compute karo aur cache karo; ranking ko background me refresh karo.
  • Privacy: har post ki audience check karni hoti hai (public/friends/only me) — feed me galat audience ki post kabhi nahi aani chahiye.
SOURCESource: designs/facebook-newsfeed.md
23System Designs

Facebook Messenger

Facebook Messenger — real-time 1-to-1 aur group chat: messages turant pahunchein, read receipts dikhein, aur saare devices par sync hon. Challenge: real-time delivery + message history ka scale.

Repo note: Messenger ka design SUMMARY.md ki list me nahi hai, lekin repo me uski file (designs/facebook-messenger.md) aur 2 diagrams maujood hain — isliye ye section bhi shamil hai. File me sirf diagrams hain, likha hua design nahi hai.

Requirements

  • Functional: 1-to-1 aur group messages bhejo; text, photo, video, stickers; read receipts aur typing indicator; message history dekho; multiple devices par sync.
  • Non-functional: messages real-time me deliver hon (milliseconds); high availability; messages kabhi khoyengi nahi; massive scale — billions of messages per day.

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me: client → LB → chat servers → message queue → storage + push to receiver. Message bhejte hi chat server use queue me daalta hai aur receiver ko push karta hai (agar online hai to WebSocket se, warna push notification).

Diagram walkthrough — Detailed design

  • Connection: har online user ka chat server se persistent WebSocket connection hota hai — message aate hi turant deliver hota hai.
  • Message flow: sender → chat server → message queue (durability ke liye) → message store (history) → receiver ke chat server → receiver. Queue isliye taaki receiver offline ho to message khoye nahi — online aate hi deliver ho jaye.
  • Ordering: har conversation me messages ka order bana rehna chahiye — per-conversation sequence number se (ek conversation ke messages ek hi partition/shard par jayein).
  • Sync: ek user ke saare devices par same history — har device apna last-seen message ID batata hai, server uske baad ke messages bhej deta hai.
  • Read receipts: receiver ne message padha to sender ko receipt jati hai — ye bhi ek message ki tarah queue se jata hai.

Data model

EntityFields
Messagemessage_id, conversation_id, sender_id, text/media URL, created_at, sequence_no
Conversationconversation_id, participant_ids, last_message, updated_at

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Connections: millions of concurrent WebSocket connections — connection servers ko horizontally scale karo, aur user-to-server mapping service discovery se rakho.
  • Storage: message history bahut badi hoti hai — conversation_id par shard karo, purani history cold storage me.
  • Group chats: ek message N participants ko jata hai — fanout ko async workers se karo.
  • Ordering vs availability: partition ke time order thoda gadbad ho sakta hai — client sequence number se sort karke dikhata hai.
SOURCESource: designs/facebook-messenger.md
24System Designs

Yelp

Yelp — local businesses dhoondhna: "mere aas-paas ke achhe restaurants" search karo, reviews padho, photos dekho. Challenge: location-based search — lakhon businesses me se kareeb wale dhoondhna, fast.

Repo note: Repo ki Yelp wali file me sirf 1 diagram hai (overview) — detail diagram repo me nahi hai. Neeche overview diagram samjhaya gaya hai.

Requirements

  • Functional: location + keyword se businesses search karo ("pizza near me"); business page (photos, reviews, rating, hours); review likho; photos upload karo.
  • Non-functional: search fast ho (100ms ke andar); location accurate ho; massive scale — millions of businesses aur reviews.

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me: search query → LB → search service → geo-index + business store → ranked results. Location search ka core geospatial index hai — businesses ko unki latitude/longitude ke hisaab se index kiya jata hai.

Location search kaise kaam karta hai

  • Geohash: latitude/longitude ko ek short string (geohash) me convert karo — paas wali jagahon ke geohash prefix same hote hain. Search karte time user ke geohash ke aas-paas wale cells ke businesses lao.
  • Quadtree / R-tree: map ko chaar hisson me baanto, har hisse ko aur chaar me — jis hisse me user hai, uske businesses lao. Yelp-scale par geohash zyada common hai.
  • Ranking: distance + rating + review count + relevance (keyword match) — in sabko mila kar score banao.
  • Reviews: business ke reviews alag store me (business_id par partition); rating ko aggregate karke cache me rakho — har read par saare reviews ginna nahi padta.

Data model

EntityFields
Businessbusiness_id, name, category, lat, lng, geohash, address, hours
Reviewreview_id, business_id, user_id, rating, text, created_at
Photophoto_id, business_id, storage URL

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Geo-index: poori duniya ka index ek machine par nahi aata — geohash prefix par shard karo.
  • Hot areas: bade sheheron me businesses zyada — un cells ke shards par load zyada; shards ko aur chhota karo (finer geohash).
  • Reviews: popular business ke lakhon reviews — pagination + top reviews cache karo.
SOURCESource: designs/yelp.md
25System Designs

Uber Backend

Uber Backend — rider ko kareeb ke driver se match karna aur trip ko track karna. Challenge: real-time location — lakhon drivers ki location har second update hoti hai, aur rider ko seconds me match chahiye.

Repo note: Repo ki Uber wali file me sirf 1 diagram hai (overview) — detail diagram repo me nahi hai. Neeche overview diagram samjhaya gaya hai.

Requirements

  • Functional: rider ride request kare; kareeb ke available drivers dhoondho aur match karo; driver accept kare; trip ko live track karo; fare calculate karo; payment karo; rating do.
  • Non-functional: matching seconds me ho; location updates real-time hon; massive scale — millions of concurrent drivers/riders; surge pricing bhi handle karo.

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me: rider app + driver app → LB → matching service → geo-index (driver locations) + trip service → payments. Driver ki location har kuch seconds me update hoti hai aur geo-index me jati hai; rider request aate hi matching service us area ke available drivers dhoondhta hai.

Matching kaise kaam karta hai

  • Driver location index: drivers ki live location geohash/quad-tree index me rakho — rider ke aas-paas (jaise 3 km radius) ke available drivers turant mil jayein.
  • Dispatch: kareeb ke drivers ko ride offer karo; pehle accept karne wale ko trip do; koi accept na kare to radius badhao (aur drivers dhoondho).
  • Trip state machine: requested → matched → driver arriving → trip started → trip ended → payment → rating. Har state change event ke roop me store hota hai.
  • Surge pricing: ek area me demand supply se zyada ho to price multiplier badhao — ye demand aur supply ka real-time ratio hai.
  • ETA: driver se rider tak ka time — road network + live traffic se calculate karo (mapping service).

Data model

EntityFields
Driver locationdriver_id, lat, lng, geohash, status (available/busy), updated_at
Triptrip_id, rider_id, driver_id, pickup, drop, fare, status, created_at
Paymenttrip_id, amount, method, status

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Location updates: lakhon drivers × har 3 second — in-memory geo-index (Redis Geo) me rakho, database me har update mat likho.
  • Matching latency: geo-index se kareeb ke drivers milliseconds me milne chahiye; dispatch ko async queue se karo.
  • Hot areas: airport/stadium jaise jagah par drivers aur riders dono zyada — un geohash cells ke shards ko alag se scale karo.
  • Consistency: ek driver ko ek hi trip mile — dispatch me distributed lock ya atomic claim use karo.
SOURCESource: designs/uber-backend.md
26System Designs

Ticketmaster

Ticketmaster — events ke tickets bechna: user event dhoondhe, seat chune, payment kare, ticket paye. Challenge: high-demand event par ek hi seat do logon ko mat becho — aur flash sale me lakhon users ek saath aayein to system down mat ho.

Repo note: Repo ki Ticketmaster wali file me sirf 1 diagram hai (overview) — detail diagram repo me nahi hai. Neeche overview diagram samjhaya gaya hai.

Requirements

  • Functional: events search karo; venue ka seat map dekho; seat select karo aur hold karo; payment karo; ticket (QR/e-ticket) pao; waitlist join karo (sold out ho to).
  • Non-functional: ek seat sirf ek baar bechni hai (overselling kabhi nahi); flash sale me high concurrency handle karo; payment reliable ho.

Diagram walkthrough — Overview

Overview me: user → LB → booking service → seat inventory (lock) → payment service → ticket service. Seat select karte hi wo seat temporarily hold ho jati hai (jaise 10 minute ke liye) — tab tak koi aur use nahi le sakta.

Seat booking kaise kaam karta hai

  • Seat hold: user seat chune to seat ko 10 minute ke liye hold karo (in-memory lock ya DB row lock). Time khatam ho aur payment na ho to hold chhodo — seat wapas available.
  • Inventory: har event ki seats ka inventory ek hi jagah se manage karo (shard per event) — taaki do users ko ek hi seat na mile. Overselling rokne ke liye seat status ka single source of truth rakho.
  • Queue (virtual waiting room): flash sale me lakhon users aayein to sabko ek saath andar mat aane do — virtual queue me rakho aur baari-baari andar aane do. Isse system crash nahi hota.
  • Payment: payment hone ke baad hi ticket confirm karo; payment fail ho to hold chhodo. Idempotency key se double-charge roko.
  • Ticket: confirm hone par unique ticket (QR code) generate karo; ticket ko transfer bhi kiya ja sakta hai.

Data model

EntityFields
Eventevent_id, name, venue_id, date, total_seats
Seatseat_id, event_id, section, row, number, status (available/held/sold), held_until
Bookingbooking_id, user_id, event_id, seat_ids, amount, status, created_at

Scaling aur bottlenecks

  • Concurrency: ek seat par hazaaron log — distributed lock ya event-sharded inventory se ek hi winner chuno.
  • Flash sale: virtual queue + rate limiting; cache se event/seat-map reads serve karo (writes hi bottleneck hain).
  • Payment failures: payment slow ho to holds expire hone lagenge — hold time aur payment timeout ko balance karo.
SOURCESource: designs/ticketmaster.md
27Interview Preparation

Starting Point — Kahan se Shuru Karein

System design seekhne ka sabse achha tareeka hai pehle broad overview lena — phir basics, phir designs. Repo ye lectures aur resources starting point ke roop me deta hai. Inhe dekhne ke baad tumhe pata chalega ki aise systems kaise sochte hain.

Starting point — Lectures aur resources

  • System Design video series (YouTube playlist) — simple cheezon se shuru hoti hai (load balancing, message queues) aur phir poore systems banane tak jati hai (WhatsApp aur Tinder jaise systems). Playlist kholo
  • Scalability talk (Harvard CS75) — scalability ki broad overview ke liye bahut useful. Talk dekho
  • Scaling Up talk (Udacity course) — web applications ko scale karne par. Talk dekho
  • Scalability for Dummies — scalability ki basic concepts par articles ka collection. Articles padho
  • Designing Data-Intensive Applications (book) — repo kehta hai ye large-scale systems aur unhe banate time aane wali practical challenges par sabse behtareen kitabon me se ek hai. Ye data-oriented applications par focused hai.

Ye talks tumhe ek starting point dengi ki aise problems ke baare me kaise sochna hai. Baaki lectures bhi dekh sakte ho agar zaroorat ho.

Repo note: Upar wale resources ke naam aur links repo ke README se liye gaye hain; vyaktiyon ke naam visible text se hataye gaye hain, links wahi hain.
SOURCESource: README.md
28Interview Preparation

Pehle Ye Basics Seekho

Designs par jaane se pehle in topics ki decent samajh honi chahiye — kisi khaas order me nahi, lekin sab par ek basic grip zaroori hai.

  1. Operating system basics — file system, virtual memory, paging, instruction execution cycle kaise kaam karte hain. Shuruaat ke liye OS ki standard textbook kaafi hai; agar pehle se decent knowledge hai to ek advanced OS textbook try karo.
  2. Networking basics — kam se kam TCP/IP stack, Internet, HTTP aur TCP/IP ki basics aani chahiye. Scalability wali pehli lecture se broad overview mil jayegi. Networking ki ek mashhoor textbook hai "Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach" — repo use recommend karta hai.
  3. Concurrency basics — threads, processes, aur apni language me threading. Locks, mutex aadi aane chahiye.
  4. DB basics — DB ke types (SQL vs NoSQL aadi), hashing aur indexing, EAV-based databases, sharding, databases ke liye caching, master-slave aadi.
  5. Basic web architecture ka idea — load balancers, proxy, servers, database servers, caching servers, precompute, logging, big data aadi — broadly pata ho ki har layer kis liye hai.
  6. CAP theorem ka basic summary — kabhi seedha theorem par sawaal nahi poochha gaya, lekin ise jaanna large-scale systems design karne me madad karta hai. (CAP Theorem wala section 11 dekho.)
SOURCESource: README.md
29Interview Preparation

Interview me Kaise Jawab Dein

System design questions ka jawab dene ka ek process hota hai — use seekh lo to koi bhi question structured tareeke se handle kar sakte ho.

Kahan se seekhein

  • System design approach videos (hiredintech) — repo kehta hai ye shuruaat ke liye excellent jagah hai. Approach ye hai: pehle system ke use-cases clear karo, phir abstract tareeke se components aur unke interactions ke baare me socho, phir bottlenecks ke baare me socho aur ye tay karo ki tumhare system ke liye kya zyada critical hai (jaise latency vs reliability vs uptime), aur apne approach ke trade-offs ke saath unhe address karo. Videos dekho
  • System design — Cracking the Coding Interview approach — ek chhote use-case ko pehle solve karke phir system ko expand karne ka tareeka. Book dekho

Practice hi ekmatra rasta hai

Prepare karne ka sabse achha tareeka hai mock interviews karna: koi bhi topic lo (neeche Common Design Questions dekho), design banane ki koshish karo, phir jaakar dekho ki wo aise kyun design kiya gaya hai. Iska koi alternative nahi hai! Whiteboard par system design karna asal me code likhne aur test karne jaisa hai — sirf padhne se tum ek hadd tak hi aage badhoge.

SOURCESource: README.md
30Interview Preparation

9 Steps — Mera Approach

Repo ke author ne bataya hai ki wo interviews me mentally kin steps se guzarta hai — ye steps uske actual interview experiences par based hain. Inhe apna template bana lo.

  1. Bilkul sure raho ki problem kya poochhi ja rahi hai — assume karne se pehle onset par hi clarify karo.
  2. Use-cases — ye critical hai: system kis kaam ke liye use hoga, kis scale par use hoga, ye zaroor jaano. Constraints bhi: requests per second, request types, data written per second, data read per second.
  3. Problem ko bahut chhote set ke liye solve karo — jaise 100 users ke liye. Isse data structures, components aur overall model ka abstract design samajh me aayega.
  4. Components likho — ab tak mile saare components aur unke interactions likh do.
  5. Rule of thumb — kam se kam ye 8 cheezein yaad rakho:
    • Processing aur servers
    • Storage
    • Caching
    • Concurrency aur communication
    • Security
    • Load balancing aur proxy
    • CDN
    • Monetization — agar relevant ho to, kaise monetize karoge?

    Jaise: kis tarah ki DB chahiye (kya Postgres kaafi hai, nahi to kyun?), caching chahiye aur kitni, kya security prime concern hai?

  6. Special cases — us question ke khaas cases. Jaise thumbnails store karne ka system design kar rahe ho to kya file system kaafi hoga? Facebook ya Google ke scale par kya hoga? Kya NoSQL-based database kaam karega?
  7. Minor optimizations — components jagah par aane ke baad, use-cases ke hisaab se kai jagah chhoti optimizations dhoondho aur trade-offs batao jo 99% cases me better scaling me madad karein.
  8. Scaling out ya up — horizontal vs vertical scaling ka decision lo (architecture issues wala article padho).
  9. Interviewer se check karo — kya koi aur special case hai jo wo solve karwana chahta hai? Aur jis company me interview de rahe ho, uski architecture jaanna bahut madad karta hai — questions aam taur par usi domain ke honge, aur tumhara prior knowledge kaam aayega.
SOURCESource: README.md
31Interview Preparation

Common Design Questions

Ye questions tumhare level aur role par depend karte hain, lekin ye sabse frequently poochhe jaane wale design questions hain. Har ek par 45 minute ka timer laga kar practice karo.

  1. Amazon ki "frequently viewed products" page design karo — jaise last 5 dekhi gayi items dikhane wala page. (Hint: user activity ka recent list — cache + fast reads.)
  2. Multiplayer online poker game design karo — persistence, concurrency aur scale solve karo; ER diagram banao.
  3. URL compression system design karo. (Short URL wala section 14 dekho.)
  4. Search engine design karo — basic crawling, collection, hashing aadi. Domain knowledge wale logon se aam taur par poochha jata hai.
  5. Dropbox ki architecture design karo. (Section 17 dekho.)
  6. Picture sharing website design karo — thumbnails aur photos kaise store karoge? CDNs ka use? Har layer par caching?
  7. News feed design karo (Facebook, Twitter jaisi). (Section 22 dekho.)
  8. Maps par based product design karo — jaise location dekar hotel ya ATM finder.
  9. malloc, free aur garbage collection system design karo — kaun se data structures use karoge? Malloc par decorator pattern?
  10. Price comparison site design karo — jaise e-commerce websites par availability aur price compare karna. Kab cache karoge, kitna query karoge, e-commerce sites par efficiently crawl kaise karoge, databases ki sharding, basic database design.
  11. Instant messaging web application design karo — jaise WhatsApp ya Facebook chat. Har ek ki issues, scaling problems, status aur availability notification.
  12. Ek document par simultaneously collaborate karne ka system design karo — jaise Google Docs (operational transformation / CRDT).
  13. Running stream of data ke top 'n' ya most frequent items design karo — (Hint: count-min sketch + heap.)
  14. Election Commission ki architecture design karo — counting day par desh bhar ke lakhon voting booths se votes collect karke real-time me batana hai ki kaun si party kitni seats par aage hai. Har booth ki voting machine network se connect hokar {[party_id, num_votes], ...} array return karti hai.
  15. Logging system design karo — bahut saare servers same application chala rahe hon, saamne load balancer ho. Kisi bhi server par exception aaye to alarm chahiye — logs me specific words ("Exception", "Disk Full" aadi) dikhein to system ko detect karna hai. (Bonus question — repo me 14 ke baad ye bhi hai.)
SOURCESource: README.md
32Interview Preparation

Architectures Jo Dekhni Chahiye

Repo ke author ne personally in architectures ko dekha tha — ye real systems hain jinhe padhne se scale ka intuition banta hai.

  • Basics of Google Search — search engine kaise kaam karta hai, crawling se ranking tak. Paper padho
  • Messaging frameworks — Kafka aur RabbitMQ jaise queuing architectures ki basics.
  • Redis, MongoDB, Cassandra — inka broad overview aur advantages.
  • Google File System — Google ka distributed file system (GFS paper). Paper padho
  • Google Architecture — Google ke systems ki high-level architecture. Article padho
  • Instagram architecture — image-based social network kaise scale hota hai. Article padho
  • Memcache scaling by Facebook — Facebook ne memcached ko kaise scale kiya (research paper). Paper padho
  • Twitter scaling — Twitter ke scale ki kahani (video). Video dekho
  • Facebook Graph API (TAO) — Facebook ka distributed datastore. Paper padho
  • Facebook Haystack (photo storage) — photos store karne ki needle/haystack architecture. Paper padho
  • YouTube architecture aur video optimizations — video kaise serve hoti hai (video). Video dekho

34Interview Preparation

Low on Time? (TL;DR)

Repo khud kehta hai: shortcut mat lo — system design practice se seekha jata hai, shortcut short term me madad karega lekin interview ke baad is link par wapas aakar in-depth samajhna. Lekin agar interview ek hafte me hai, to ye karo:

  1. Scalability wali lectures aur Udacity ke links se guzro (Starting Point wala section 27 dekho).
  2. Jis company me interview de rahe ho, uska engineering blog padho (ya startup hai to uske sabse kareeb wali company ka blog).
  3. System design process wali talk dekho aur jawab dene ka process develop karo (How to Answer wala section 29 dekho).
  4. Ye terms yaad rakho — interview me apne dimaag me in par roll karte raho, aur relevant lage to mention karo:
    • Processing aur servers
    • Storage
    • Caching
    • Concurrency aur communication
    • Security
    • Load balancing aur proxy
    • CDN
    • Monetization

Best of luck! — aur repo me contribute karna ho to pull requests bhej sakte ho.

Lab 1: Consistent Hashing Ring Simulator

Simple hashing (key % n) aur consistent hashing ka farq khud dekh lo — server jodo aur gino kitni keys move hoti hain.

Result
Ring banane ke liye button dabao.
LABYe lab is SPA ke sections par aadharit hai — har control ke peeche wala concept uske apne section me detail me diya hai.
LInteractive Lab

Lab 2: Cache Eviction Simulator (LRU / LFU / FIFO)

Ek request sequence do, cache size aur policy chuno — dekho kitne hits aur kitne misses hote hain.

Result
Sequence daalo aur Simulate dabao.
LABYe lab is SPA ke sections par aadharit hai — har control ke peeche wala concept uske apne section me detail me diya hai.
LInteractive Lab

Lab 3: Load Balancer Simulator

Round robin, weighted round robin, least connections aur IP hash — ek hi traffic par chaaro algorithms chalakar distribution compare karo.
